```{r, loadpackages}
#| echo: false
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(httr2)
library(gt)
library(rvest)
```

```{r, createaccesstoken}
#| echo: false
#| include: false
# Define client ID and client secret in order to generate Spotify access token
client_id <- Sys.getenv("SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID")
client_secret <- Sys.getenv("SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET")

# Generate Spotify access token
req_access_token <- request("https://accounts.spotify.com/api/token") |> 
  req_method("POST") |> 
  req_body_raw(paste0(
    "grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=",
    client_id,
    "&client_secret=",
    client_secret
  ), "application/x-www-form-urlencoded") |> 
  req_perform() |> 
  resp_body_json()
spotify_access_token <- req_access_token$access_token
```

```{r, gettthplaylist}
#| echo: false
#| include: false
# Scrape kworb.net for the Spotify Global Daily chart.
# NOTE: We used to fetch the editorial playlist "Today's Top Hits" 
# (37i9dQZF1DXcBWIGoYBM5M) plus /audio-analysis for each track, but both
# endpoints were restricted by Spotify's Nov 2024 Web API changes for 
# third-party apps. kworb aggregates Spotify's own chart daily and provides 
# the underlying track IDs, so we can still enrich each row via the 
# /v1/tracks endpoint (which remains available).
kworb_url <- "https://kworb.net/spotify/country/global_daily.html"
kworb_page <- read_html(kworb_url)
kworb_rows <- kworb_page |> html_element("table") |> html_elements("tr")
kworb_rows <- kworb_rows[-1]  # drop header

parse_kworb_row <- function(row) {
  tds <- html_elements(row, "td")
  title_cell <- tds[[3]]
  links <- html_elements(title_cell, "a")
  hrefs <- html_attr(links, "href")
  track_href <- hrefs[grepl("/track/", hrefs)][1]
  artist_href <- hrefs[grepl("/artist/", hrefs)][1]
  tibble(
    position    = as.integer(html_text(tds[[1]])),
    pos_change  = html_text(tds[[2]]),
    artist_name = html_text(links[grepl("/artist/", hrefs)][1]),
    song_name   = html_text(links[grepl("/track/", hrefs)][1]),
    song_id     = sub("^.*/track/([^./]+)\\.html$", "\\1", track_href),
    artist_id   = sub("^.*/artist/([^./]+)\\.html$", "\\1", artist_href),
    streams_today = html_text(tds[[7]])
  )
}

top_hits_df <- bind_rows(lapply(head(kworb_rows, 50), parse_kworb_row))

# Batch enrich with Spotify track metadata (up to 50 IDs per call).
tracks_resp <- request("https://api.spotify.com/v1/tracks") |> 
  req_url_query(ids = paste(top_hits_df$song_id, collapse = ",")) |> 
  req_headers(Authorization = paste0("Bearer ", spotify_access_token)) |> 
  req_perform() |> 
  resp_body_json()

enriched <- tibble(
  song_id        = vapply(tracks_resp$tracks, function(x) x$id %||% NA_character_, character(1)),
  album_art      = vapply(tracks_resp$tracks, function(x) x$album$images[[1]]$url %||% NA_character_, character(1)),
  track_duration = vapply(tracks_resp$tracks, function(x) x$duration_ms %||% NA_integer_, integer(1)),
  popularity     = vapply(tracks_resp$tracks, function(x) x$popularity %||% NA_integer_, integer(1))
)

top_hits_df <- top_hits_df |> left_join(enriched, by = "song_id")
```

```{r, createtable}
#| expandable: false
generate_svg_circle <- function(popularity_value) {
  popularity_value <- as.numeric(popularity_value)
  
  # Calculate the radius of the circle
  radius <- 10 + 15 * (popularity_value / 100)  
  
  # Interpolate the color from red (popularity = 0) to green (popularity = 100)
  circle_colour_picker <- colorRampPalette(c("#B91d1d", "#ED8E11", "#EDDE11", "#1DB954"))
  
  # There are 101 colour values since popularity ranges from 0 to 100
  color <- circle_colour_picker(101)[popularity_value + 1]
  
  # Generate the SVG code for the circle
  svg_code <- sprintf(
    '<svg height="%1$s" width="%1$s"><circle cx="%2$s" cy="%2$s" r="%2$s" stroke="none" stroke-width="0" fill="%3$s" /><text class="circle-text" x="%2$s" y="%2$s" font-size="%4$s" fill="white" text-anchor="middle" dy=".3em">%5$s</text></svg>',
    2 * radius,        # SVG width and height
    radius,            # Circle center x, y
    color,             # Fill color used also for stroke
    radius * 0.6,      # Font size based on radius
    popularity_value   # Text to display
  )
  return(svg_code)
}

# Create the gt table with custom formatting
top_hits_df |>
  select(position, album_art, song_name, artist_name, track_duration, popularity) |>
  gt(id = "custom") |>
  cols_label(
    position = md("**#**"),
    album_art = md("**Song**"),
    song_name = "",
    artist_name = md("**Artist**"),
    track_duration = html('<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" x="0px" y="0px" width="15" height="15" viewBox="0,0,255.998,255.998"><g fill="#ffffff" fill-rule="nonzero" stroke="none" stroke-width="1" stroke-linecap="butt" stroke-linejoin="miter" stroke-miterlimit="10" stroke-dasharray="" stroke-dashoffset="0" font-family="none" font-weight="none" font-size="none" text-anchor="none" style="mix-blend-mode: normal"><g transform="scale(10.66667,10.66667)"><path d="M12,2c-5.523,0 -10,4.477 -10,10c0,5.523 4.477,10 10,10c5.523,0 10,-4.477 10,-10c0,-5.523 -4.477,-10 -10,-10zM14.586,16l-3.293,-3.293c-0.188,-0.188 -0.293,-0.442 -0.293,-0.707v-5c0,-0.552 0.448,-1 1,-1v0c0.552,0 1,0.448 1,1v4.586l3,3c0.39,0.39 0.39,1.024 0,1.414v0c-0.39,0.39 -1.024,0.39 -1.414,0z"></path></g></g></svg>'),
    popularity = md("**Popularity**")
  ) |>
  text_transform(
    locations = cells_body(columns = album_art),
    fn = function(x) { web_image(url = x, height = 50) }
  ) |>
  text_transform(
    fn = function(x) {
      generate_svg_circle(x)
    },
    locations = cells_body(columns = popularity)
  ) |> 
  fmt(
    columns = track_duration, 
    fns = function(x) {
      num_minutes <- floor(x / 60000)
      num_seconds <- ifelse(round((x %% 60000) / 1000) == 60, 59, round((x %% 60000) / 1000))
      sprintf("%d:%02d", num_minutes, num_seconds)
    }
  ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = c(position, popularity)
  ) |> 
  tab_footnote(
    footnote = "The popularity of a track is a value between 0 and 100, with 100 being the most popular. The popularity is calculated by algorithm and is based, in the most part, on the total number of plays the track has had and how recent those plays are.
Generally speaking, songs that are being played a lot now will have a higher popularity than songs that were played a lot in the past.",
    locations = cells_column_labels(columns = popularity)
  ) |> 
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = md("**Source:** [kworb.net Spotify Global Daily Chart](https://kworb.net/spotify/country/global_daily.html), enriched with the Spotify Web API `/v1/tracks` endpoint.")
  ) |> 
  tab_options(
    table.font.color = "#FFFFFF",
    table.background.color = "#191414",
    table.font.size = px(12),
    table.border.top.color = "transparent",
    table.border.bottom.color = "transparent",
    table_body.hlines.color = "transparent",
    table_body.border.bottom.color = "transparent",
    column_labels.border.bottom.color = "transparent",
    column_labels.border.top.color = "transparent",
    footnotes.background.color = "#282828",
    source_notes.background.color = "#282828"
  ) |> 
  tab_style_body(
    style = cell_borders(
      sides = c("top", "bottom"),
      weight = px(0) # Remove row borders
    ),
    fn = function(x) { is.numeric(x) | is.character(x) }
  ) |> 
  opt_css(
    css = "
    table tr:nth-child(odd) {
      background-color: #282828;
    }
      
    table tr:hover {
      background-color: #383838;
    }
    
    .cell-output-display {
      overflow-x: unset !important;
    }
    
    div#custom {
      overflow-x: unset !important;
      overflow-y: unset !important;
    }
    
    #custom .gt_col_heading {
      position: sticky !important;
      top: -5px !important;
      z-index: 10 !important;
    }

    /* Make every table row look clickable */
    #custom .gt_table tbody tr {
      cursor: pointer;
    }

    /* Highlight the currently-playing row */
    #custom .gt_table tbody tr.now-playing {
      background-color: #1DB954 !important;
      color: #191414 !important;
    }
    #custom .gt_table tbody tr.now-playing a { color: #191414 !important; }
    "
  )
```

### Row {height="15%"}

```{ojs}
//| expandable: false

// Transpose the R data frame into an array of row objects usable in OJS
top_hits = transpose(top_hits_ojs)

// Reactive state: which row is currently selected.
// Starts at position #1 and is updated by (a) clicking a table row or
// (b) changing the dropdown.
mutable selectedIndex = 0

// Dropdown stays as a secondary way to jump to a song.
viewof songDropdown = Inputs.select(
  top_hits.map((d, i) => ({ label: `${d.position}. ${d.song_name} \u2014 ${d.artist_name}`, value: i })),
  {
    label: "Now playing",
    format: o => o.label,
    value: { label: `${top_hits[0].position}. ${top_hits[0].song_name} \u2014 ${top_hits[0].artist_name}`, value: 0 }
  }
)

// Keep the dropdown in sync with whatever row is selected (click or dropdown).
{
  mutable selectedIndex = songDropdown.value;
  return null;
}

// Attach row click handlers once the gt table is in the DOM.
// We re-find rows on every run so OJS reactivity works after hot reloads.
clickWiring = {
  // Defer until after the gt table has been painted.
  await new Promise(r => requestAnimationFrame(() => setTimeout(r, 50)));
  const rows = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll("#custom .gt_table tbody tr"));
  rows.forEach((tr, i) => {
    tr.onclick = () => { mutable selectedIndex = i; };
  });
  return rows.length;
}

// Visually mark the currently-playing row.
highlightRow = {
  const rows = document.querySelectorAll("#custom .gt_table tbody tr");
  rows.forEach(r => r.classList.remove("now-playing"));
  if (rows[selectedIndex]) rows[selectedIndex].classList.add("now-playing");
  return selectedIndex;
}

// Current track, derived.
currentTrack = top_hits[selectedIndex]
```

```{ojs}
</div>`
```
